Regulatory Friction

Rules that fragment a market or stop it forming at all.

What it looks like Illustrative scenario

A graphene supercapacitor startup has working units and cannot sell one without a safety certification priced at four hundred thousand dollars, a process written for firms a hundred times its size. The buyers exist. The certifier's timetable, not the technology, decides whether the market exists.

Scenario: The Certification Bridge

How an AI intervention works AI Risk Insulation · AI Input Translation

Regulation rarely says no outright. It says not in this form, not in that jurisdiction, not without this document. The interventions read the rulebook as data: input translation extracts the compliance attributes a deal needs from the parties' own documents, semantic matching applies only the rules that hold where each side sits, and risk insulation watches the registries so a contract can carry a compliant exit or fallback when a permit or standard changes mid-deal. The rule stays. The paralysis goes.

How traditional markets cope

  • Specialist who knows the codeuntil the specialist's fee exceeds the deal
  • Certification bodies and standardsuntil the standard was written for firms a hundred times larger
  • Trading inside one jurisdictionuntil the buyer is across the border
